newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh-Iran oil swaps may start Jan '97 - minister.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh-Iran oil swaps may start Jan '97 - minister.

text.p: Kazakh Oil and Gas Minister Nurlan Balgimbayev said on Monday that a scheme in which Kazakhstan and Iran will undertake to swap two million tonnes of crude oil a year could start in January, 1997.
"The deal might start at the beginning of next month (January, 1997)," Balgimbayev told reporters while attending a session of parliament in the Kazakh capital Almaty.
An official delegation travelled to Tehran last week to hammer out final details on the deal.
Earlier this month, Balgimbayev said the scheme would start with volumes of around two million tonnes annually but said the amount could increase to six million tonnes a year.
Kazakhstan would ship its oil across the Caspian Sea to Iran's Caspian Sea coast. In turn, Iran would provide the equivalent amount of crude at its Gulf ports.

The United States, which has imposed sanctions against Iran over what it views as the country's record on terrorism, views the deal with concern as some of its own oil majors are investing in Kazakh oil projects.
Kazakhstan has said that only state-owned oil, and not output from Western companies, will be part of the swaps.
The Central Asian country is anxious to break its reliance on neighbouring Russia to the north for oil exports.
Russia has made available only limited capacity in its own pipeline network for Kazakh oil exports which are set to soar in the next decade.
